title: Pocket Calculator
statement: An old pocket calculator uses postfix order: numbers come first and the operator after them, so `3 4 +` means 3 + 4. You get the key presses as an array `tokens` of whole numbers and the operators `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`. Each operator uses the two most recent results, in order (the earlier one first). Division drops the fraction toward zero. Return the final result.
constraints: The expression is valid and never divides by zero
Every result fits in a 32-bit integer

answerKey.pattern: Stack of numbers; an operator pops two and pushes the result
keyPoints: For an operator, pop b (the top) and then a, compute a op b, push the result
Order matters for - and /: the earlier number is a
Division truncates toward zero (Math.trunc in JavaScript)
The one number left is the answer

hints: When an operator arrives, which two numbers does it use?
The two most recent results are on top of a stack. Pop the second operand first.
Compute a op b with a popped second, push the result, and keep going.
